To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular composition and the relative estrogen-binding capacity of the estrogen receptor in human breast tumors are highly variable and that the molecular species of the receptor are related to the clinical outcome of patients treated with hormonal therapy.

molecular heterogeneity of the estrogen receptors exists in cytosols prepared from human breast tumors and that the ionic charge of the estrogen receptor is related to the clinical outcome of patients receiving endocrine therapy.

estrogen receptors from human mammary carcinoma cytosols are heterogeneous with regard to molecular size and surface charge, and that the 8S estrogen receptor from hormonally sensitive breast carcinomas is more heterogeneous than that from hormonally insensitive breast tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heterogeneity of the estrogen receptors of human breast carcinomas.
the molecular composition of estrogen receptors in human breast carcinomas.
the heterogeneity of the 8 and 4S species of estrogen receptor in human breast tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one single molecular form of the estrogen receptors that is responsible for the responsiveness of human breast tumors to endocrine therapy.

there is a great deal of heterogeneity of the estrogen receptors in the cytosols from breast tumors and that this heterogeneity may be of clinical significance in the management of patients with advanced breast cancer.
the molecular forms of cytoplasmic estrogen receptors from human mammary tumors are more complex than has been previously recognized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 8S estrogen receptor is composed of at least five components and that the 4S receptor is composed of two components.
the molecular heterogeneity of the 8s form of estrogen receptors in human breast cancer may be an important determinant of response to hormonal therapy.
the 8S estrogen receptor is a complex mixture of components that may vary in their molecular size, surface charge, and binding capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular composition is not a good predictor of response to hormonal therapy.
there are multiple forms of estrogen receptors in human breast cancers.
the molecular heterogeneity of the estrogen receptor in breast cancer is not a static phenomenon but is subject to changes in the tumor cell population.
